title: Rollout heuristics daybook and safety appendix (Nov 2026)
body:
Purpose:
- Working daybook for a small-batch rollout of model-routing/fallback changes across hosted + dedicated clusters. This is a working scratchpad for the week-of rollout: heuristics, tempo gates, quick smoke queries, and a safety appendix with rollback triggers.

High-level goals:
- Validate model routing polyfill in production without increasing p99 latency by >10%.
- Observe traffic handoffs across regions and confirm cache/KV warmup behavior.
- Ensure automatic fallback engages and degrades gracefully under capacity spikes.

Rollout tempo heuristics (principles):
- Heartbeat windows: 15m micro-watches during initial traffic shifts, expand to 1h cadence after 6 consecutive green windows.
- Increment size: start at 0.5% of traffic, double cadence each green window up to 8% then switch to linear +5% every 30m.
- Conservative triggers: any sustained p50 increase >15ms or p99 >50ms for 3 consecutive windows => pause and evaluate.
- Noise tolerance: allow one noisy window during peak minute bursts; require trend across 3 windows for decisions.

Day-by-day calendar (week-of rollout):
- Day 0 (prep, Fri): final smoke environment run, verify canary test-suite (see checklist below), distribute runbook to ops channel.
- Day 1 (Mon 09:00 UTC): open 0.5% shift to region A (US-west), 15m heartbeat for first hour.
- Day 1 (Mon 12:00 UTC): if green, expand to 2% and open read-only replay in staging-to-prod path.
- Day 2 (Tue): ramp to 8% across US regions, start telemetry sampling for reranks and prompt-level latency.
- Day 3 (Wed): introduce dedicated pool routing test for customers with reserved capacity (watch tail latency and allocation errors).
- Day 4 (Thu): A/B compare quality and regression metrics on live prompt set.
- Day 5 (Fri): decide go/no-go for global roll to EU-1 (if no safety flags).

Preflight checklist (must pass before Day 1):
- [ ] Canary build promoted and pinned to tag: release/rr-routing-2026-11-11.
- [ ] Observability dashboards: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, 429s, CPU/GPU spillover visible for each pool.
- [ ] Telemetry queries pre-saved and validated (examples below).
- [ ] Runbook and rollback play posted to #release-ops and #sre-watch.
- [ ] Oncall rota: primary/secondary/engineer-on-call assigned for the full rollout window.

Canary smoke tests (quick):
- Local smoke: deploy to canary node, run 100 synthetic requests of mixed sequence lengths (32/128/512).
- KV warmup: send repeated prefix requests to validate cache hit rate > 85% within 2 minutes.
- Failover test: simulate removing a worker and confirm fallback latency < 2x baseline and no errors >0.5%.
- Throughput soak: 10m at target QPS for canary capacity, check no worker restarts.

Immediate rollback triggers (safety appendix):
- Latency: sustained p99 increase >2x baseline for 30+ minutes.
- Error burst: >0.5% of requests returning 5xx or corrupt structured outputs for 3 consecutive windows.
- Cost shock: sudden token billing spike >40% predicted (indicates runaway rerender/looping).
- Functional regression: automated regression eval fails for >2 critical prompt sets (regression delta threshold configured in Optimize).
- Unrecoverable resource thrash: autoscaler thrashing (scale up/down >4x in 15m).

Rollback steps (fast):
1) Pause rollout and set traffic split to last-known-good model variant (API: PATCH /routing/policy -> config: previous).
2) Spin up emergency lane by redirecting to fallback region (if capacity available) or disable the new routing feature flag.
3) Notify #release-ops, #eng-sre, and customer success; open incident channel if >10% customers impacted.
4) Collect artifacts: telemetry windows (15m prior to trigger), synthetic request traces, and sampling of degraded responses.
5) Triage with oncall + eng leads, prepare hotfix if root cause is code; otherwise schedule rollback and postmortem.

Telemetry quick queries (to paste into metrics UI):
- p99 latency by model_variant over last 60m, 1m rollup.
- error_rate{code=5xx} by region and pool filtered to routing-change-tag=rr-2026-11.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio by shard (expect >80% after warmup).
- tokens_per_request mean and 95th percentile (watch sudden increases).
- sample traces: filter by request_tag=rr-test and status!=ok limit 200.

Release notes (draft - short form):
- Release: Routing & fallback orchestration improvements (rr-routing-2026-11).
- Summary: Adds model-variant-aware routing policies, improved fallback heuristics, and KV warmup prioritization to reduce cold-start latency for short sequences.
- Impact: expected incremental latency improvement for cached prefixes; initial rollout gated by traffic splits. No changes to customer-visible API contract.
- Known issues: under heavy churn, some dedicated pools may exhibit transient allocation lag (will be throttled by tempo gates).
- Rollback instructions: see "Immediate rollback triggers" section.

Open questions / decisions:
- Q1: Should we enable aggressive KV prefetch for dedicated only or for hosted as well? leaning dedicated-first.
- Q2: Do we want to enable 1% of EU traffic as an overnight test before full EU roll? ops prefers daytime testing.
- Q3: Telemetry retention for this experiment - 14 days should be sufficient, confirm with observability.

Action items (owners):
- Evan: finalize PR and tag release; update runbook; publish short blurb to #release-notices (due Fri EOD).
- Maya: prepare A/B prompt sets and schedule quality run on Wed.
- Liam: update dashboards and save queries; validate synthetic runner.
- Priya: coordinate with customer success for any VIP customers on Dedicated capacity (email list prepared).

Notes to self:
- Keep the first 3 windows really close; humans read p99 spikes differently than dashboards. If in doubt, pause.
- Capture one full trace for each deviation event with headers and prompt content (redact PII).
- Don't trust one-off noisy samples during peak traffic - watch for trend.

Appendix: quick paste commands and links:
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2789 (can revert via revert PR if needed).
- Tracing: trace.redwood.internal/query?tag=rr-2026-11 (save link in dashboard).
- Incident template: confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=incident-template

End of day checklist (for the oncall to confirm after each shift):
- [ ] Traffic split stable and within expected %
- [ ] No alert escalations in last 30m
- [ ] Telemetry snapshots archived to experiment bucket
- [ ] Rollback artifact bundle uploaded (if triggered)

-- scratchpad footer --
This doc is a living daybook; update timestamps in the calendar and checklists as we iterate during the week. If we hit a non-trivial rollback, convert this into the incident postmortem draft with attached artifacts.
